content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text weighs a collision between the defender's and challenger's cases as chain against chain by footing, which is exactly the kind of collision-weighing K-C governs.", "verdict": "CLEAN", "quote": "the challenger's seed/loins chain is footed but does not name Joseph as the begetter; the defender's chain is footed but rests on the woman-route inference", "rule_words": "the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side", "room": "The rule's retired 'stating-verse test': I weighed whether the judge's phrase 'does not name Joseph as the begetter' demands that some one verse state Joseph's begetting in its own words (the retired test, a breach) or notes that the chain read together never reaches Joseph as begetter (a footing gap, permitted); the footing reading fits because the judge grants that chain 'is footed' and weighs both sides symmetrically by what each chain rests on.", "why": "The judge decides by comparing the two chains' footing — footed, one not reaching Joseph, one resting on an inference — and never lets the absence or presence of a single stating verse decide, so K-C is obeyed."}
